# A round-up interval as an interval of the default type

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/*/brute/, results/brute-code.json and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `upward_to_interval_1` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

A kernel of the round-up interval ([its kernels](upward.md)), of the opt-in header `kairn/upward.hpp`, which `kairn/kairn.hpp` does not include and which requires the options of [The round-up interval](../concepts/upward.md) (GCC and Clang `-frounding-math`, MSVC `/fp:strict`). No operation of it rounds: it gives the same result in every rounding mode.

## What it computes

The same set in the other storage: a state of the round-up interval, $X = [-x_n, x_u]$ stored as $(x_u, x_n)$, as an interval of the default type, $Z = [z_l, z_u]$; the empty set, both lanes a NaN, as the empty set, $(+\infty, -\infty)$. Exact: the same members:

$$Z = X.$$

A state of the round-up interval is stored as its upper bound and its lower bound negated, the two lanes of one register: $X$ as $(x_u, x_n)$ ([its kernels](upward.md#the-stored-pair)).

## C++

**Not yet called by the public headers.** No public operation computes this kernel yet.

## Requires

- $X = [-x_n, x_u]$, stored as $(x_u, x_n)$, is a canonical state of the round-up interval: the empty set, both lanes a NaN; or a nonempty interval, each lane a number of `T` or $+\infty$ (neither a NaN nor $-\infty$), with $-x_n \le x_u$; its members are the real numbers between $-x_n$ and $x_u$.

## Guarantees

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- The result $Z = [z_l, z_u]$ is a canonical interval.
- $Z$ is the empty set, $(+\infty, -\infty)$, exactly when $X$ is empty.
- $Z$ and $X$ have the same members; so for a nonempty $X$ the same bounds, $z_l = -x_n$ and $z_u = x_u$, exactly, as extended real numbers (a zero bound may change its sign).

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit, no operation of the kernel rounding, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `upward_to_interval_1_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/IeeeUpwardExact.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/IeeeUpwardExact.v), against `upward_to_interval_1_spec`, the statement the generator prints from these claims into [`proofs/gen/UpwardStatements.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/UpwardStatements.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions upward_to_interval_1_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/UpwardAudit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/UpwardAudit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `upward_to_interval_1_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** the negated lower bound negated, and the upper bound, the empty set after a test (the listing of the round-up interval). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/upward_to_interval_1.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/upward_to_interval_1.kernel), the description the C++ (`include/kairn/gen/upward.hpp`) and the formal model (`proofs/gen/UpwardModel.v`) are generated from. Each statement is one operation of `T`, and none rounds to nearest ([the round-up interval in the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-round-up-interval)); `unord(a, b)` is whether $a$ or $b$ is a NaN.

```
# A state of the round-up interval as a default interval Interval<T, 1> (docs/developer/design/upward.md,
# "Conversions"): [-n, u], and the empty set (NaN, NaN) as the default empty set (+inf, -inf). Exact,
# in every rounding mode: the same set, the signs of zero bounds aside. Requires the rounding mode
# upward set by kairn::upward::Scope and the options of docs/concepts/upward.md (GCC and Clang
# -frounding-math, MSVC /fp:strict).

e  = unord(xu, xu)
nl = neg(xn)
mi = neg(const inf)
zl = select(e, const inf, nl)
zu = select(e, mi, xu)
```

## Measured

No stored brute-force run has judged this kernel yet.

## Not claimed

- Anything for operands that do not satisfy the requirements.
- The sign of a zero limb, and which NaN a NaN result is: the claims compare neither.
- What the compiled code gives where its environment is not the one of the statement: no flush to zero of results or operands (its result does not depend on the rounding mode). That is the program's to make so, as [The round-up interval](../concepts/upward.md#what-the-program-guarantees) says, and no proof covers that step ([What is not machine-checked](../concepts/correctness.md#what-is-not-machine-checked)).
